items.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: And it was Thad Jones that caused it to become peaceful.

ctx.x: Well you know Dizzy’s band was a pretty wild band. We was pretty wild in Dizzy Gillespie’s band. And now here I’m in a society band, you know I mean you set up everything, you didn’t slouch or nothing in your chair or nothing, and you set up in Lunceford’s band because everyone came out of the university where you know it’s been taught, in Nashville, Tennessee. Can’t think this minute. But anyway, we’re playing for the Queen now, and I’m just getting in the band now, and I hadn’t been in the band but a

week, and now we’re playing for the Queen, and we’re in line, here’s the Count Basie’s band, here’s Mario Bauza, and over here is Judy Garland, and here standing alongside are The Rockettes. And here one of the Rockettes was kind of whispering, “where’s the party tonight?” And now they’re playing “America” [hums], and we’re at attention here. But then when it was over, ready for his [inaudible] I says, “just meet me back stage and we’ll talk about where the party will be.” And, but, somebody heard this voice and…
